Comments: Onsite for an incident response to a reported release from the operator. The release was reported today at 10:11am. The release occurred as a result of a 210bbl steel tank 2" plug failure located at the bottom of the tank. It is estimated that a total of 50bbls was lost from the tank. The release migrated within the dike and into the substrate of the earthen dike. An unknown amount of fluid seeped through and traveled over the dike wall which migrated approximately 60+/- yards down gradient from the dike. The impacted area outside of the dike is being excavated and stockpiled inside the dike waiting on a roll-off container for disposal. The earthen dike area is designed in a manner with two levels, the oil tanks are located at a higher elevation than the brine storage tanks. The release did not enter a waterway. Cleanup will continue at the site. Violations are noted

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/06/2022 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Cummings Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/06/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 960901
Permit API: 081-20386
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cummings Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/06/2022
Comments: On July 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at the Range Resources Ogontz 3H, 7-9H due to a reported spill of production fluid (CTS 365323). Range Resources Kirby Steck reported a spill of approximately 2 barrels of production fluid to the well pad surface and off the pad on July 6, 2022. A water tanker back latch was not completely sealed and when they were adding production fluid to the tank it started leaking and spilled onto the pad surface and over the pad slope to low spot off the southeast end of the pad. The area of impact off the pad was about 60 ft. by 10ft and about 6 inches in depth. On the well pad surface the impact was approximately 15 ft. by 15 ft and Range Resources had only scraped the top layer of stone to remove the impacted soil. The fill slope of the pad had a 4 foot wide area of impact from the top of the slope to the bottom of the slope which is approximately 10 ft. long. Later in the day on July 6, 2022, Mr. Steck left a message with DEP stating that after removing all the impacted soil that the volume of the spill of production fluid was closer to 3 barrels. The contaminated soil was being stored on separate containment from the plugging operations. Range Resources was waiting for covered dumpsters to arrive onsite. Moody is scheduled to be onsite on July 8, 2022 to collect confirmatory samples and begin the Act 2 process.The spill of production fluid outside of containment and onto the well pad surface and off the well pad is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 8226587
Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/24/2025
Comments: On March 24, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release. Present during today's inspection was operator representative Ronald Seich.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. All other production equipment was observed removed and loaded/being loaded onto a trailer for disposal.It appeared excavation had been started in the area where the production equipment was removed. Excavated material/soil was observed loaded onto tarps. No excavation appeared to have been started on the ditch. Mr. Seich stated that they planned on having all excavation completed, including the ditch, by the end of the day. He also stated that Moody would be onsite tomorrow (3/25/2022) to perform a site assessment and collect samples to evaluate their remediation.A soil conductivity reading was taken in the area where the production tank was previously located with a reading of 0.34mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of 16.00mS, 9.16mS, 2.30mS, 0.87mS, 0.83mS, and 0.80mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. A conductivity reading was taken in this area of the ditch with a reading of 0.34mSA conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.73mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings obtained, it appears that the conductivity readings are comparable to the previous inspections in regards to distance and levels of elevated readings in the ditch. It appears that released fluids may have been contained to the portions of the ditch where standing fluid was observed, and it did not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.Bases on today's inspection, violations remain outstanding.

Upon arrival there was no well at the original coordinates 40.041485, 79.664770 as seen in photograph 8. Two potential wells were located. Comments: On August 2, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill report. The spill was called in to the Department today at 9:54 AM by the Operator, who described a 25-26 barrel release of crude oil that was found by a well tender at 8:40 AM. Operator will be utilizing Act 2 standards for clean up.The Department arrived on site at approximately 1:15 PM and spoke with Paul Steiner of Diversified. According to Steiner, a well tender discovered the release at approximately 8:40 AM from a crack (Photo 3) in the storage/production tank on site. Steiner approximated the total release to be 26 barrels based on the amount of crude oil in the production tank last week (approximately 4 feet) and the amount of crude oil still in the tank at discovery, which is an approximate 22 inches.The release migrated towards and past the production equipment (Photo 4) and down an embankment, where it reportedly stopped at a berm (Photo 8) according to Steiner. Steiner is using a PID meter to detect the extent of the oil's migration. During the on site inspection, Diversified was excavating impacted material at the berm and moving it upslope so that they can place it into a Spartan dump truck to have it transported for disposal. Steiner says one truck load will be transported tonight, excavation will stop, then another Spartan truck will arrive tomorrow morning, excavation will resume, and remaining impacted material will be taken off site before Moody arrives in the afternoon to confirm complete site clean up. Oil absorbent booms will be placed around and downslope of the impacted material overnight tonight to prevent further migration between truck loads, according to Steiner.Following the inspection, Steiner and myself spoke with DCNR Park Manager Kris Baker of Keystone State Park at the park office to notify the park of the release.Violations issued for spill. The Department requests disposal documents when made available.

Inspection Date: 2020-01-27
Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Report Details

Violation Code: OGA3215(F) - WELL LOCATION RESTRICTIONS -FLOODPLAINS - Failure to follow requirements for a well site in a floodplain, floodway or flood fringe.
Violation ID: 8284093
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/05/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/05/2025
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8248043
Permit API: 123-47821
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/05/2025
Comments: The Loomis B Lease Loomis 7 OG well is the closest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the Loomis B lease. At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the Loomis 7 OG well. The Loomis B tank battery consists of two stock tanks, a produced fluids separator, and one subsurface produced fluids tank located inside earthen containment diking. The conventional wells on this lease were being produced at the time of this inspection. After arriving on the lease I began to inspect the condition of the tank battery. I found that the produced fluids separator and stock tanks in containment were equipped with PVC drain lines to separate any produced fluids that enter the tank battery from either the separator or the stock tanks into the subsurface produced fluids tank. At the time of this inspection, only the PVC drain line connected to the separator was found to be draining produced fluids. At the time of this inspection, the flowing PVC drain line was improperly positioned, as it was straddled on the edge of a cutout hole on the top of the subsurface produced fluids tank. The manner in which the drain line was situated allows the majority of the fluids flowing through the line to be released onto the top of the tank and ultimately onto the floor of the containment area, as opposed to inside the subsurface tank.The specific conductance of the accumulated fluid inside of the containment area measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. The soils below the fluid accumulating in the containment area also measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. A visual inspection of the containment area revealed additional signs of staining and stressed/dead vegetation around the produced fluids tank similar to that resulting from the ongoing release. This evidence is an indication of previous releases inside of the containment area prior to this inspection. At the time of this inspection, it did not appear that the pooling of fluids around the subsurface produced fluids tank were accumulating at a rate consistent with the volume of fluids being released into containment by the PVC drain. This and the evidence of stressed vegetation/oil staining around the proximity of the subsurface produced fluids tank referenced above suggests that the released fluids inside of the containment area are migrating into the soil below. A conservative estimate of a one gallon per minute discharge rate over the greater than 90 minute duration that I was present to observe the release suggests that more than 90 gallons (>2bbl) were released into the containment during this inspection.Sample number 4568-004 was collected from the fluid actively flowing from the PVC drain line and sample number 4568-005 was collected from the accumulated fluids inside of the containment area adjacent the subsurface produced fluids tank. These samples were sent to the DEP lab for SAC 942 analyses. After concluding my inspection, I called Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) at 14:59 and requested that he meet me immediately on the lease. Upon his arrival, I informed Kyle that I discovered a problem with the tank battery. I gestured to the ongoing release of fluids from the improperly placed PVC drain line. Kyle immediately placed the drain line into the cutout in the subsurface produced fluids tank. Kyle then phoned another TMP official to inform them of the release, but indicated that neither he or the other TMP official seemed to be aware of who had pumped the wells on this lease today. I informed Kyle that the release of fluids would be documented in this inspection report and that a Notice of Violations (NOV) would be included.A NOV is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: On 10/10/2023, I conducted an inspection due to an incident that occurred on 10/06/2023. A gathering line inside of the tank battery containment which is located 290 feet to the south from the Arnold #2, had failed and crude oil traveled down slope from the tank battery area, aprox. 90 feet away. A neighbor had complained to the pumper, reporting that they smelled gas on Wednesday October 5th or Thursday October 6th. The pumper had looked around and found nothing on those days. On the evening of Friday October 6th crude was discovered inside and outside the containment. Sam Harvey of Bull Run notified the Department of the release on the Arnold lease owned by Armac Resources on Saturday October 7th.The gathering line ran through the dike wall, it is not clear whether the dike wall failed or if the line leaked outside of containment or both. Crude oil is visible outside of containment. When I arrived on site, the area as seen in the photos was already mulched and seeded. I removed several patches of mulch and smelled the soil underneath he mulch, the soil had a strong distinct smell of crude oil. The southwest side of the dike wall has been excavated and the contaminated material was placed inside of a roll off that remains onsite. It is unclear how much if any soil has been removed in the downslope area below the tank battery.There is no evidence of production fluid in the road ditch located along Bauer Hill road. A boom has been placed in the dry ditch as a precaution. I spoke with Sam Harvey and Justin Hansen of Bull Run (who are contract pumping and facilitating the clean up for Armac Resources). I suggested that an underflow dam be placed at the bottom of the area that has been mulched (base of hill), this is to prevent any remaining production fluid from being washed down to the road side ditch of Bauer Hill which leads to an unnamed tributary of Glade Run.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8184834
Permit API: 125-28816
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Cecil Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024 the Department conducted an inspection of the Augustine George 11039 access road located in Cecil Township, Washington County in regards to a complaint received on 04/24/24 CTS # 380091. The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspection, a truck was observed opening a valve and releasing what appeared to be freshwater onto the access road. Upon investigating this release, John Hulsey of Range Resources informed the Department that this fluid is freshwater and that the purpose of releasing said freshwater is to minimize the amount of dust caused from vehicles traveling up and down the access road. The released freshwater mixed with sediment as it flowed down the access road on to N Depaoli Road, traveled along the shoulder of N Depaoli and flowed off the shoulder into according to the site plans, an unnamed intermittent tributary to Millers Run. properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to BEAR LAKE PROP LLC in Columbus Township, Warren County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/25/2024 to BEAR LAKE PROP LLC in Columbus Township, Warren county. CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEAR LAKE PROP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/25/2024
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8206012
Permit API: 123-39874
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Columbus Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/25/2024
Comments: The Bittinger 4 disposal injection well is housed inside a shed and is plumbed directly to the Bear Lake Properties, LLC truck unloading area located approximately 1500 feet east of the Bittinger 4 well. Multiple pieces of liner have been placed on the floor of the shed around the well. At this time, standing fluid was visible on the liner. A conductivity meter was used to find that the fluid's conductivity was greater than 20,000 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The partially exposed dirt floor at the edge of the liner was found to have soils with conductivity greater than 1,000 uS/cm, with some measurements as high as 2,500 uS/cm being observed. The fluid originating from Bittinger 4 traveled southwest from the shed to the edge of the gravel well pad, as evident from the dead vegetation and exposed soils in this direction. The portion of the gravel pad downslope of the shed was noticeably wet despite recent lack of rain. Approximately three feet southwest of the shed, a conductivity reading of 4,000 uS/cm was observed a few inches below the surface of the gravel. Approximately 70 feet southwest of the shed, soil conductivity of 2,330 uS/cm was observed in soils at the edge of the gravel pad.Background soil conductivity measurements were taken across portions of the site in areas that appeared to be unaffected by the release of fluids from Bittinger 4. Background soil conductivity readings between 200 to 300 uS/cm were observed at apparently unimpacted areas near the Bittinger 4 location.After encountering a depression at the edge of the gravel pad, the flow of the fluid was redirected southward. The southward flow was apparent via swaths of dead vegetation and bare soils that appeared to broaden in size and meander about following the terrain. This anastomosing continued for approximately 250 feet between the edge of the gravel pad to where a utility pole was located downslope of Bittinger 4. Near the utility pole, the flow of fluid again channelized and continued approximately 250 feet further down an ATV trail. At this point, as observed by dead vegetation, the majority of the released fluids crossed over the ATV trail and entered a natural drainage swale.Standing water in the drainage swale was found to have an elevated conductivity of 6,100 uS/cm. Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

However, they still lack secondary containment, as is required at unconventional well sites (see photos 2, 4, and 5). The top hatch of the production tank closest to the well head closest to the well head was observed on the ground. The Department recommends that this top hatch is replaced onto the production tank to prevent possible overflowing with rainwater (see photo 6).The well postings on-site include contact information for Murphy Production, Inc. The Department recommends that equipment onsite that is not in use for production is removed from site.The access road is stabilized with gravel. The well is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (see photos 3 and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued under IR 3484420 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Comments: Today I conducted a routine inspection at the Varner 2 well. The access road was maintained and in good condition. The well head was maintain with no leaks or defects observed. Production tanks in good condition and were inside containment at the compressor station. No leaks or defects observed at the compressor stations equipment. The site is currently producing.During the inspection I discovered a slide on the Northside of the Varner 2 pad. The slip appeared to be a minor slide where the top soil slid off the slope. The size is approximately 40 feet in length x 15 feet in width. The slide exposed the slopes rock and dirt allowing for erosion. The well pads geo mat/ liner was also exposed at the edges. Comments: On March 27, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the Shotski 7H well in Somerset Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 3/25/2023. The report indicted that approximately 5-10 gallons of production fluid was released from a washed out pipe within GPU 7.The Act 9 site ID, PPC plan and ER plan were on site.At the time of inspection the Operator was decommissioning the GPUs. According to the on site representative the GPUs will be removed from the location and replaced.I observed staining and excavation around the 7H GPU. I utilized a conductivity probe to collect readings within the impacted area (photos 7,8 and 9).The impacted area appeared to be approximately 20' wide and 40' long and 2 to 12 inched in depth. The 7H GPU did not appear to be contained within secondary containment. The Shotski wells are not included within the 12/17/2020 Secondary Containment COA. I also collected a conductivity reading within the 7H self contained GPU (photo 13).The release appears to be contained to the well pad surface. Violation are being issued for failure to control a regulated fluid and failure to design and construct the well site with secondary containment.

Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)
